blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: We investigate whether state-of-the-art large language models (LLMs) generate feedback that reflects the pedagogical practices of expert teachers in terms of feedback focus and adaptivity. Previous evaluation efforts have examined feedback characteristics, its impact on learning, and its target, yet the focus of feedback and its adaptivity remains largely overlooked. To bridge this gap, we adopt and refine Narciss’s taxonomy into seven feedback focus types to annotate teacher and LLM-generated feedback across three university writing courses. We release FeedType , a benchmark containing annotated teacher and LLM feedback from six LLMs under three prompting strategies. We assess the coverage and distribution of feedback focus types, and examine whether LLMs adapt their feedback across draft stages and student performance levels as an expert instructor does. Our findings show that while most LLMs cover most feedback focus types, they fail to reflect teacher feedback distributions and show varying levels of adaptivity, with none matching the teachers’ adaptive behavior. We believe FeedType will support future research on pedagogical alignment in LLM feedback generation.
blocks.zh: 我们调查最先进的大型语言模型是否产生反馈,反映专家教师在反馈重点和适应性方面的教学做法。 以往的评价工作审查了反馈特征、其对学习的影响及其目标,但反馈的重点和适应性在很大程度上仍然被忽视。 为了弥合这一差距,我们将纳西斯的分类学引入并完善为七种反馈焦点类型,以在三个大学写作课程中对教师和LLM产生的反馈进行注释。 我们发布FeedType, 包含六位LLM的附加说明的老师和LLM反馈, 我们评估反馈重点类型的覆盖面和分布情况,并研究法学硕士是否像专家教员那样,在起草阶段和学生成绩水平上调整其反馈。 我们的研究结果显示,虽然大多数LLMS涵盖了大部分反馈焦点类型,但它们未能反映教师的反馈分布,并显示出不同程度的适应性,没有任何一个符合教师的适应行为。 我们相信FeedType将支持未来在LLM反馈生成方面对教学一致性的研究.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Large language models (LLMs) have emerged as promising tools for providing personalized feedback on student essays at scale, with recent work demonstrating success across creative Rashkin et al. (2025) , second language Wang et al. (2025b) , and academic Steiss et al. (2024) writing. However, research across multiple educational tasks, including tutoring Tack and Piech (2022) , math problem solving Macina et al. (2023) and essay feedback Dai et al. (2023) has shown that LLMs fail to capture the pedagogical practices expert teachers use to guide student learning. For example, in tutoring, Macina et al. (2023) found that ChatGPT tends to provide direct answers, while expert teachers guide students through hints. This has motivated research on pedagogical alignment Macina et al. (2023) ; Macina et al. (2025) ; Sonkar et al. (2024) ; Maurya et al. (2025) , which measures how well LLM behavior aligns with expert teaching Perczel et al. (2025) .
blocks.zh: 大型语言模型(LLMs)已成为提供规模化学生论文个性化反馈的有希望的工具,近期的作品展现了跨越创意的Rashkin等人(2025年),第二语言Wang等人(2025年b),以及学术的Steiss等人的成功. (2024)写作. 然而,涉及多种教育任务的研究,包括辅导Tack和Piech(2022年)、解决Macina等人的数学问题(2023年)和论文反馈Dai等人(2023年)都表明,LLMs未能掌握指导学生学习的教学做法专家教师。 例如,在辅导中,Macina等人(2023年)发现ChatGPT倾向于提供直接的答案,而专家教师则通过提示指导学生. 这激发了对教学调整Macina等人(2023年)、Macina等人(2025年)、Sonkar等人(2024年)、Maurya等人(2025年)的研究,这些研究衡量了LLM行为如何与专家教授Perczel等人(2025年)相一致。

blocks.en:
Recently, a growing body of work has begun incorporating pedagogical dimensions into LLM-generated feedback evaluation, drawing from established feedback models that characterize effective teacher feedback Hattie and Timperley (2007) ; Yang and Carless (2013) . For example, Seßler et al. (2025) and Dai et al. (2023) applied Hattie and Timperley (2007) ’s framework, examining feedback’s learning supportive components and who feedback targets. Mah et al. (2025) applied Yang and Carless (2013) ’s framework, focusing on how feedback is delivered across cognitive, social, and structural dimensions.
However, feedback focus – what teachers focus on when responding to student writing Yu and Lee (2014) ; Yu (2014) ; Lipnevich and Panadero (2021) , remains unexplored. This is important since teachers vary their feedback focus to address different aspects of student writing Lipnevich and Panadero (2021) , yet LLMs have shown limited ability to identify writing issues Rashkin et al. (2025) ; Seßler et al. (2025) , motivating us to examine what feedback focus types LLMs tend to provide and how this compares to expert teachers.
blocks.zh:
最近,越来越多的工作开始将教学层面纳入LLM产生的反馈评价,这些评价借鉴了既定的反馈模型,这些模型是教师有效反馈哈蒂和蒂姆佩利(2007年)的特点;Yang和Carless(2013年)。 例如,Seßler等人(2025年)和Dai等人. (2023年)应用了哈蒂和蒂姆佩利(2007年)的框架,审查反馈的学习支持部分,谁的反馈目标. Mah等人(2025年)运用了Yang和Carless(2013年)的框架,
然而,反馈焦点 — — 教师在回应学生写作Yu和Lee(2014年)时关注的内容; Yu (2014); Lipnevich and Panadero (2021), 仍然未探索. 这一点很重要,因为教师为了解决学生写作Lipnevich和Panadero(2021年)的不同方面,而LLMs在识别Rashkin等人(2025年)的写作问题的能力有限;Seßler等人(2025年),激励我们审查LLMs倾向于提供的反馈焦点类型以及如何与专家教师进行比较。

blocks.en: The feedback literature has classified feedback focus into different levels, ranging from broad distinctions such as content versus form Ferris (1997) to more detailed taxonomies distinguishing specific types such as mistakes, tasks, and concepts Narciss (2008b) . Recognizing multiple feedback focus types is pedagogically important, as it informs what to address, for whom, and when. Expert teachers leverage this knowledge by shifting their focus across draft stages and adapting to each student’s individual needs Ortmeier-Hooper (2006) ; Ferris (1997) , reflecting a deeply adaptive teaching practice. To our knowledge, feedback focus has not been examined in the evaluation of LLM-generated feedback, specifically in terms of what aspects LLMs tend to focus on and whether they exhibit the same adaptive behavior across draft stages and student performance levels. We aim to bridge this gap by addressing three research questions: RQ1: What feedback focus types do LLMs tend to generate, and how does this compare to expert teachers? RQ2: Do LLMs adapt their feedback focus across draft stages, as an expert teacher does? RQ3: Do LLMs adapt their feedback focus based on student performance, as an expert teacher does?
blocks.zh: 反馈文献将反馈焦点分为不同层次,从内容与形式Ferris(1997年)等广义区分,到区分错误,任务,概念Narciss(2008年b)等特定类型更为详细的分类. 承认多种反馈重点类型在教学上很重要,因为它说明应处理什么问题,针对谁,何时。 专家教师利用这一知识,将重点转移到起草阶段,并适应每个学生的个人需求。 据我们所知,在评价LLM产生的反馈时没有审查反馈重点,具体而言,是LLMs倾向于关注哪些方面,以及它们在起草阶段和学生成绩水平上是否表现出同样的适应行为。 我们的目标是通过解决三个研究问题来弥补这一差距: 问题1: LLMs倾向于产生什么样的反馈焦点类型,这与专家教师有何比较? RQ2: LLMS是否像专家教师那样,在起草阶段调整其反馈重点? RQ3:LLMS是否像一位专家教师那样,根据学生的表现调整其反馈重点?

blocks.en:
To address these questions, we present FeedType 1 1 1 Data
available at https://github.com/nia135/FeedType . , a dataset of expert teacher feedback on student essays across three university writing courses (taken from the publicly available SEFORA corpus Oskoui et al. (2026) ), with teacher and LLM-generated feedback annotated for feedback focus.
While SEFORA provides rich teacher feedback data, it lacks feedback focus annotations needed to address our research questions. To bridge this gap, we adapt an existing taxonomy Narciss (2008b) and annotate all feedback comments in FeedType according to feedback focus. We then prompt six LLMs, covering open and closed weight models as well as the LearnLM specialized pedagogical model Team et al. (2024) , to generate feedback on selected paragraphs from FeedType using three prompting strategies. We annotate the LLM generated feedback using the same taxonomy applied to teacher feedback, enabling a direct comparison. FeedType thus serves as a benchmark for analyzing LLM pedagogical practices in terms of feedback focus and whether it adapts to student performance and draft stage. Our findings indicate that while most LLMs cover the majority of feedback focus types, they fail to reflect teacher feedback distributions and show limited adaptivity across draft stages and student performance levels.

blocks.en: LLMs have been used for feedback generation across multiple writing contexts, including L2 learner writing Wang et al. (2025b) ; Kaneko and Okazaki (2024) ; Mizumoto et al. (2024) , creative writing Rashkin et al. (2025) , and academic writing Chu et al. (2026) . Feedback generation has been explored at the sentence level Mizumoto et al. (2024) ; Song et al. (2024) ; Kaneko and Okazaki (2024) ; Bannò et al. (2024) and on complete student essays Chu et al. (2026) ; Behzad et al. (2024a) ; Rashkin et al. (2025) . However, to our knowledge, feedback generation at the paragraph level has received very little attention, despite evidence that this is a common and valuable form of expert teacher feedback Mah et al. (2025) ; Hyland and Hyland (2006) ; Zamel (1985) that LLMs fail to provide Mah et al. (2025) . We address this gap by generating paragraph level feedback across multiple writing domains (L2 learner writing, composition, and fiction), where we provide LLMs with the complete student essay and target specific paragraphs within it for feedback generation.

(2026) (中文(简体) ). 在句子层面,Mizumoto等人(2024年),Song等人(2024年),Kaneko和Okazaki(2024年),Bannò等人(2024年),以及完整的学生散文集Chu等人(2026年),Behzad等人(2024年a年),Rashkin等人(2025年)等都探讨了反馈生成问题. 然而,据我们所知,段落一级的反馈生成很少受到关注,尽管有证据表明,这是教师对Mah等人的一种常见和有价值的专家反馈形式(2025年);Hyland和Hyland(2006年);Zamel(1985年),LLMs未能提供Mah等人(2025年)。 我们通过在多个写作领域(L2学习者写作、组成和虚构)生成段落级反馈来弥补这一差距,我们在那里向LLMS提供完整的学生论文,并针对其中的特定段落进行反馈生成。

blocks.en: Many studies have evaluated LLM-generated feedback in terms of accuracy Yoon et al. (2023) , quality Algobaei and Alzain (2026) , and bias Du et al. (2025) ; Tan et al. (2026b) . Fewer have examined its alignment with expert teacher practices. In student writing, prior work has compared LLM and teacher generated feedback in terms of quality Steiss et al. (2024) , content and targets Dai et al. (2023) , and diversity Tan et al. (2026a) . We extend prior work on alignment in two ways. First, we examine feedback focus and its adaptivity, dimensions that have received limited attention in prior evaluations. Second, we compare the distribution of feedback focus types between teachers and LLMs using population-level evaluation approaches adopted in prior educational research Mah et al. (2025) ; Kucheria et al. (2025) ; Asano et al. (2025) .
blocks.zh: 许多研究从准确度Yoon等人(2023年),质量Algobaei和Alzain(2026年),以及偏差Du等人(2025年)等方面评价了LLM产生的反馈;Tan等人(2026年b). 很少有人审查了与专家教师做法的一致性。 在学生写作中,之前的工作比较了LLM,老师在质量Steiss等人(2024年),内容和目标Dai等人(2023年),多样性Tan等人(2026年a年)等方面产生了反馈. 我们以两种方式延长了先前关于调整的工作。 首先,我们审查反馈重点及其适应性,这些方面在以前的评价中得到的关注有限。 其次,我们利用以前教育研究Mah等人(2025年)、Kucheria等人(2025年)、Asano等人(2025年)所采用的人口评价方法,对教师和法学硕士的反馈重点类型分布进行比较。

blocks.en: Prior work has classified feedback focus narrowly, either by grammatical error types or limited broad categories Nagata et al. (2020) ; Steiss et al. (2024) ; Liu et al. (2025) . To address this gap, we adopt and refine the taxonomy of Narciss (2008b) , which captures a broader range of feedback focus types observed in expert teacher feedback. This taxonomy allows us to examine how teachers adapt their feedback priorities across draft stages and learner performance levels. For example, early drafts may receive greater attention to content and ideas, whereas later drafts may focus more on vocabulary and style Zamel (1985) . Similarly, feedback may differ by learner performance level Ferris (1997) because students at different levels may benefit from different types of feedback. We refer to these adjustments in feedback focus as feedback adaptivity. To our knowledge, no prior work has examined whether LLMs demonstrate similar adaptive patterns.
blocks.zh: 先前的工作对反馈焦点进行了狭义分类,有的按语法错误类型分类,有的按有限大类分类为Nagata等人(2020年);有的按Steiss等人(2024年);有的按刘等人(2025年)分类. 为了弥补这一差距,我们采用并完善了Narciss的分类法(2008b),其中涵盖了专家教师反馈中观察到的更广泛的反馈重点类型。 这种分类法使我们能够研究教师如何在起草阶段和学习者业绩水平上调整其反馈优先事项。 例如,早期的草案可能更多地关注内容和想法,而后来的草案则可能更注重词汇和风格Zamel(1985年)。 同样,反馈可能因学习者业绩水平Ferris(1997年)不同而不同,因为不同级别的学生可能受益于不同类型的反馈. 我们把反馈焦点中的这些调整称为反馈适应性。 据我们所知,以前的工作没有审查LLMS是否表现出类似的适应模式。

blocks.en: Across L2, native, and creative writing, existing corpora are limited to scores only without feedback Blanchard et al. (2013) ; Yannakoudakis et al. (2011) ; Geertzen et al. (2013) ; Ishikawa (2013) ; Crossley et al. (2025) ; Li et al. (2026) , sentence-level or holistic error-focused feedback Nagata et al. (2020) ; Nguyen et al. (2018) ; Behzad et al. (2024b) , multi-dimensional scoring and feedback without feedback focus type annotations Mathias and Bhattacharyya (2018) , or essay evaluation without feedback Wang et al. (2025a) ; Rashkin et al. (2025) . To our knowledge, no existing corpus jointly provides scores, revisions, teacher and automatic feedback, and feedback focus type annotations, all of which are needed to analyze feedback focus and its adaptivity across draft stages and student performance levels. We release FeedType , a corpus that provides all of these components, enabling such analysis. We summarize and compare existing datasets in Table 1 .

blocks.en:
We sampled course data from the publicly available SEFORA corpus of first-year college student essays and teacher feedback Oskoui et al. (2026) . In particular, we use the data from three different courses (composition, ESL, and fiction) from a single semester, choosing the semester with the highest student enrollment.
Where a course had multiple classes in the same semester, we included all of them.
The composition course includes two classes taught by the same instructor, while the ESL and fiction courses each consist of one class taught by different instructors. Students in the composition and ESL courses submitted up to three essays with multiple drafts, while fiction students submitted three essays without multiple drafts; in all courses, only the first draft was required. We focus on paragraph-level feedback, where each paragraph receives one teacher comment. Student grades and assignment rubrics are used to support feedback classification and adaptivity analysis. Table 2 summarizes the corpus, and Figure 1 shows a feedback example. Additional corpus details can be found in Appendix A .

blocks.en:
We base our annotation scheme on Narciss (2008b) ’s taxonomy, which provides detailed content focus types for feedback analysis. Prior frameworks either conflate content and function Hattie and Timperley (2007) ; Kulhavy and Stock (1989) or categorize content only broadly Ferris (1997) ; Yu (2014) ; Narciss’s taxonomy addresses both by treating them separately and offering more precise content focus types. We adapt and extend this taxonomy to better capture the nature of written teacher feedback, retaining relevant feedback types, refining others, and introducing new types to emphasize explanatory feedback. Appendix B presents the original and adapted taxonomies. The final taxonomy consists of seven feedback types: Task Constraints , which clarify assignment
goals and requirements; Concepts , which
explain key ideas needed to complete the task; Elaboration , which encourages students to
expand their ideas with more detail; Clarification , which asks students to
clarify unclear parts of their writing; Mistakes , which identify specific errors
in the text; Praise , which provides
encouragement or positive evaluation; and Other , which covers feedback that either does not fit any single focus type or spans multiple types simultaneously. Annotation guidelines
are provided in Appendix C , with some annotated feedback examples in Figure 1 .

Two authors iteratively developed and refined the coding manual through four pilot rounds. In each round, 50 teacher feedback comments (25 composition, 12 ESL, 13 fiction) and their associated paragraphs were randomly sampled and independently labeled. Disagreements were analyzed, and category definitions and instructions were updated to reduce ambiguity. This process continued until substantial agreement was achieved, with the final round reaching Cohen’s Kappa κ = 0.774 \kappa=0.774 Sim and Wright (2005) .
blocks.zh: 两位作者通过四轮试运行,迭代开发和完善了编码手册. 在每轮中,有50个教师反馈评论(25个组成,12个ESL,13个虚构)及其相关段落被随机抽取并独立标注. 对分歧进行了分析,并更新了类别定义和指示,以减少含糊不清之处。 这一进程一直持续到达成实质性协议,最后一轮达到科恩的Kappa = 0.774\kappa = 0.774 Sim和Wright(2005年).

blocks.en: Motivated by prior work demonstrating that LLMs can reliably annotate data at scale Tan et al. (2024) , we use them to automatically classify feedback according to our feedback focus types. We prompted six candidate models to classify the feedback (see Appendix F for the prompt) and evaluated their reliability using three methods. We constructed two evaluation datasets serving distinct purposes: (1) 100 randomly sampled feedback instances to measure inter-annotator agreement and assess whether LLM annotations can substitute for human annotators using the Alt-Test Calderon et al. (2025) , and (2) 400 feedback instances as a test set to evaluate whether conclusions drawn from LLM-generated annotations are consistent with those derived from human labels, ensuring the validity of our annotation pipeline. Gemini 2.0 Flash was selected as the annotator, passing all three evaluations: achieving a Cohen’s Kappa of 0.78 with human annotators, passing the Alt-Test, and producing conclusions consistent with those drawn from human annotations. Further details are provided in Appendix D .

blocks.en: 4.1 Generating Feedback with LLMs
blocks.zh: 4.1 用法学硕士生成反馈

blocks.en: We generated feedback using six models: Mistral-7B-Instruct, Mistral-24B-Instruct Jiang et al. (2023) , LLaMA-3.1 8B AI (2024) , Qwen2.5-70B-Instruct Hui et al. (2024) , Gemini 2 Flash Google DeepMind (2025) , and LearnLM Team et al. (2024) , covering both open and closed source instruction tuned models across different model sizes, to examine whether model size and type influence feedback practices. LearnLM is included as a specialized model fine-tuned for educational tasks Team et al. (2024) .
blocks.zh: 我们利用六种模式产生了反馈: Mistral-7B-Instruct,Mistral-24B-Instruct Jiang 等人 (2023), LLaMA-3.1 8B AI (2024), Quen2.5-70B-Instruct Hui et al. (2024),双子座2 Flash Google DeepMind (2025),以及LearnLM Team et al. (2024),涵盖开放和封闭源代码调制模型,跨不同模型大小,以检查模型大小和类型是否影响反馈实践. 将学习LM作为专门模式纳入教育任务中 Team et al. (2024) (英语).

blocks.en: Each model was prompted under three conditions: (1) zero-shot Rashkin et al. (2025) ; Stahl et al. (2024) , (2) zero-shot with the names and definitions of the feedback focus categories , as providing task specific information has been shown to improve LLM output quality Stahl et al. (2024) , and (3) few-shot with the names, definitions, and examples of each feedback focus type category , as in-context examples have been shown to improve LLM performance Brown et al. (2020) . The goal is to examine whether providing feedback type information or examples shifts model behavior toward expert teacher practices. Our prompt follows Rashkin et al. (2025) and Stahl et al. (2024) , instructing the model to act as a teacher and including the assignment rubric and task prompt. However, we designed the prompt to mirror real teacher context, which is often absent from prior work: (1) the full essay alongside the target paragraph, (2) the draft version, and (3) previously received feedback for revision and final drafts. The full prompt is in Appendix E , and Figure 1 shows example outputs.
blocks.zh: 每个模型都是在三个条件下催化的:(1) 零射Rashkin等人(2025年);Stahl等人(2024年),(2) 零射与反馈焦点类别的名称和定义,因为提供特定任务信息可以提高LLM输出质量Stahl等人(2024年),(3) 少数射与每个反馈焦点类别的名称、定义和实例,因为文中的例子可以提高LLM性能Brown等人(2020年)。 目标是审查提供反馈类型的信息或实例是否将模式行为转向专家教师做法。 我们的告示跟随Rashkin等人(2025年)和Stahl等人(2024年),指示该模型充当教师,并包括任务名称和任务告示。 然而,我们设计了反映教师真实背景的提示,以前的工作常常没有这样做:(1) 与目标段落一起的全文散文,(2) 版本草案,以及(3) 以前收到的供修订和最后草案用的反馈。 图1显示了实例产出。

blocks.en: RQ1: What feedback focus types do LLMs tend to generate, and how does this compare to expert teachers? We address this question in two parts: in terms of coverage and similarity.
blocks.zh: RQ1: LLMS倾向于产生哪些反馈焦点类型,与专家教师相比如何? 我们分两部分处理这一问题:覆盖面和相似性。

blocks.en:
(1.1) How much can LLMs cover teachers’ feedback types when responding to student essays? To understand whether each model can generate feedback across different focus types, we use the Cov_all metric, which measures how many of the seven feedback focus types a model produces. We start by analyzing the zero-shot baseline, where models receive no information about the feedback focus types. As shown in Table 3 , LearnLM, Llama-7B, and Mistral-7B achieve full coverage. However, Gemini and Mistral-24B fail to produce praise-focused feedback, while Qwen-70B does not produce the Other feedback focus type.
A model missing this feedback focus type generates feedback with only one focus per comment, while models that achieve full coverage demonstrate the ability to produce at least one comment that addresses multiple focus types simultaneously, or that is not categorizable as one of the provided focus types.
blocks.zh:
(1.1) 在回应学生的论文时, LLMS能涵盖多少教师的反馈类型? 为了了解每个模型是否能够在不同的焦点类型中产生反馈,我们使用Cov_all的度量法,衡量一个模型产生的七个反馈焦点中有多少个类型. 我们首先分析零射线基线,其中模型没有收到反馈焦点类型的信息。 如表3所示,LearnLM、Llama-7B和Mistral-7B实现了全覆盖。 然而,双子座和Mistral-24B未能产生注重赞美的反馈,而Quen-70B则不产生其他反馈焦点类型.
缺少这种反馈焦点类型的模型产生每个评论只有一个焦点的反馈,而实现全覆盖的模型则显示能够至少生成一个同时处理多个焦点类型的评论,或者不能归类为所提供的焦点类型之一.

blocks.en: To guide the models toward more complete coverage, we modified the prompting by adding information about the feedback focus types and providing few-shot examples. As shown in Table 3 , Mistral-24B benefits from both strategies - producing praise-focused feedback when prompted with either category information or examples, while Qwen-70B just benefits from examples. Gemini, however, still fails to produce praise-focused feedback across both strategies. In addition, Gemini shows degradation as it now misses the Other feedback focus type in addition to missing praise. Similarly, LearnLM, which achieved full coverage in the zero-shot baseline, begins to miss the Other feedback focus type when provided with category information, indicating that explicit category guidance may shift some models toward generating more single-focused feedback.
blocks.zh: 为了指导模型更完整地覆盖,我们修改了提示,增加了关于反馈焦点类型的信息,并提供了很少的例子。 如表3所示,Mistral-24B从这两个战略中受益——在有类别信息或实例的激励下产生注重赞扬的反馈,而Qun-70B只是从实例中受益。 然而,双子座仍然未能在两个战略中产生注重赞扬的反馈。 此外,双子座显示出退化,因为它现在除了缺少赞美之外,还错过了其他反馈焦点类型。 同样,在零射线基线中实现全覆盖的LearnLM,在得到类别信息后,开始错过其他反馈焦点类型,表明明确的类别指导可能会将一些模式转向产生更注重单一的反馈。

blocks.en: (1.2) How similar is the feedback focus type distribution of LLM-generated feedback to that of teachers? We examine how similar each model’s feedback focus type distribution is to that of teachers using JSD. As shown in Table 4 , in the zero-shot setting, LearnLM achieves the lowest JSD (0.1344), indicating the closest alignment with the teacher distribution, followed by Llama-7B (0.1619) and Mistral-24B (0.1780). Among all models, the educationally fine-tuned LearnLM most closely approximates the teacher feedback focus type distribution, while larger models such as Gemini and Qwen-70B show some of the highest divergence. Applying different prompting strategies yields limited improvement. Prompt 2 increases JSD for most models, while Prompt 3 improves alignment only for Mistral-7B (0.2398). In both cases, the zero-shot baseline remains the closest to the teacher feedback focus type distribution for most models.
blocks.zh: (1.2) LLM产生的反馈的反馈焦点类型的分布与教师的反馈如何相似? 我们研究每个模型的反馈焦点类型分布如何与使用JSD的教师相似。 如表4所示,在零镜头设定中,LearnLM实现最低的JSD(0.1344),表示与教师分布最接近,其次是Llama-7B(0.1619)和Mistral-24B(0.1780). 在所有模型中,经过教育精细调整的LearnLM最接近教师反馈焦点类型分布,而更大的模型如双子座和Quen-70B显示出一些最大的差异. 采用不同的促动战略产生的改进有限。 Express 2增加了大多数模型的JSD,而Express 3只改进了Mistral-7B(0.2398)的对齐. 在这两种情况下,零镜头基线仍然是大多数模型最接近教师反馈重点类型的分布.

blocks.en: To better understand these results, we examine the feedback focus type distribution more closely. As shown in Figure 2 , Gemini, Qwen-70B, and Mistral-7B exhibit a strong preference for Elaboration, assigning more than 50% of their feedback to this type, while Llama-7B prefers Mistakes at over 60%. This preference for a single type might explain their mostly higher divergence from the teachers, who distribute feedback more evenly. In contrast, LearnLM and Mistral-24B show no such preference, with no single type exceeding 50%, and are relatively closer to the teacher distribution. Moreover, the strong preference for a single type might lead to repetitive, narrow feedback, potentially causing models to overlook other important aspects of student writing.
blocks.zh: 为了更好地理解这些结果,我们更仔细地审查反馈焦点类型的分布. 如图2所示,双子座,Quen-70B和Mistral-7B表现出强烈的偏好,将50%以上的反馈分配给这种类型,而Llama-7B则倾向于60%以上的误差. 这种对单一类型的偏好可能说明他们与教师差异较大的原因,教师更平均地分发反馈。 相反,LearnLM和Mistral-24B没有表现出这种偏好,没有单一类型超过50%,并且相对接近教师分布. 此外,强烈倾向于单一类型可能会导致重复的、狭隘的反馈,可能导致模型忽略学生写作的其他重要方面。

blocks.en: RQ2: Do LLMs adapt their feedback focus across draft stages, as an expert teacher does? To address this question, we examine whether feedback focus type distributions change across draft versions for both the teacher and each model, using Fisher’s Exact Test to detect significant changes, where significance suggests adaptation to the student’s draft. This analysis is limited to the composition course, as the fiction course has no drafts and the ESL course was excluded due to limited variation in teacher feedback focus types.
blocks.zh: RQ2: LLMS是否像专家教师那样,在起草阶段调整其反馈重点? 为了解决这一问题,我们审查反馈重点类型的分布是否在教师和每个模式的草稿中发生变化,利用Fisher的精确测试来发现重大的改变,其中重大意义表明要适应学生的草稿。 这种分析仅限于组成课程,因为虚构课程没有草稿,而ESL课程由于教师反馈重点类型差异有限而被排除在外.

blocks.en:
Table 5 presents zero-shot results, and shows that the teacher demonstrates clear feedback adaptivity across draft stages, with significant changes in five feedback focus types: Task Constraints, Elaboration, Clarification, Mistakes, and Praise, across both stages, from initial to revision and from revision to final. When looking at the models, Mistral-24B shows the closest pattern to the teacher, with significant changes in three feedback focus types: Elaboration, Clarification, and Mistakes, across both stages. Task Constraints, however, shows a significant change only from initial to revision. Llama-7B follows, showing significant changes in two feedback focus types: Task Constraints and Mistakes, across both stages, while Elaboration shows a significant change only from initial to revision. Gemini also shows significant changes in two feedback focus types: Elaboration and Mistakes, across both stages. LearnLM shows significant changes in Mistakes across both stages, while Elaboration changes only from initial to revision.
Interestingly, all models that demonstrate adaptivity consistently show significant changes in the same two feedback focus types: Mistakes and Elaboration. This aligns with the distribution analysis in Figure 2 , where these two types appear with the highest proportion across most models. This suggests that models are more capable of adapting feedback focus types they produce frequently.
blocks.zh:
表5列出了零镜头结果,并显示教师在草稿阶段表现出明显的反馈适应性,在五个反馈重点类型方面有重大变化: 任务限制、拟订、澄清、错误和颂扬,从最初修订到最后修订。 在查看模型时,Mistral-24B显示了与老师最接近的图案,在三个反馈焦点类型上都发生了显著的变化: 精心制定,澄清,以及两个阶段的错误. 然而,任务限制表明,只是从最初改为修订。 下面是Llama-7B,显示了两种反馈焦点类型的重大变化: 任务制约和错误贯穿两个阶段,而拟订工作仅表明从初始阶段到修订阶段发生了重大变化。 双子座还显示出两种反馈焦点类型有显著变化: 细化和错误,贯穿两个阶段. 学习 LM显示两个阶段的错误都发生了重大变化,而精心拟订则只从初始阶段到修订阶段。
有趣的是,所有显示适配性的模型都一致地显示出相同两种反馈焦点类型的重大变化: 错误与精心策划. 这与图2中的分布分析一致,在图2中,这两种类型在大多数模型中所占的比例最高。 这表明模型更有能力调整它们经常产生的反馈重点类型。

blocks.en: RQ3: Do LLMs adapt their feedback focus based on student performance, as an expert teacher does? To address this question, we examine whether feedback focus type distributions differ between high- and low-performing students for both the teacher and each model, using Fisher’s Exact Test to detect significant differences, where significance suggests that feedback focus varies with student performance. This analysis is limited to the composition course, as it is the only course that provides essay grades with variation across students. For each draft stage, students are divided into high- and low-performing groups based on the median score (details in Appendix A ), and the proportion of each feedback type is computed for each group.
blocks.zh: RQ3:LLMS是否像一位专家教师那样,根据学生的表现调整其反馈重点? 为了解决这个问题,我们研究教师和每个模型的反馈焦点类型分布是否不同,利用Fisher的精确测试来发现显著的差异,其中意义表明反馈焦点随学生的表现而不同。 这一分析仅限于组成课程,因为它是唯一提供学生间差异的论文课。 对于每个草稿阶段,学生根据中位分分为高成绩组和低成绩组(详见附录A),并计算每个组的每类反馈的比例.

blocks.en: As shown in Table 6 (zero-shot), the teacher’s feedback shows significant differences between high- and low-performing students in Task Constraints and Praise. Gemini and Mistral-24B show significant differences in Clarification, LearnLM in Mistakes, and Qwen-70B in Elaboration, while Llama-7B and Mistral-7B show no significant differences across any feedback focus type. Except for Gemini, the feedback focus type that shows a significant difference corresponds to the type the model produces most frequently as in Figure 2 , suggesting that most models can only adapt to high- and low-performing students in feedback focus types they produce with sufficient frequency. Furthermore, all models that show adaptivity based on student performance are large or closed models.

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en: We present the first systematic study of LLM alignment to expert teachers at the level of feedback focus type distributions in student writing. Using a content-based feedback focus taxonomy, we annotate teacher and LLM feedback across three writing courses and evaluate six LLMs under three prompting strategies. Our findings show that while most LLMs cover most feedback focus types, they fail to reflect teacher feedback distributions. In terms of adaptivity across draft stages, the teacher shows significant changes in five feedback focus types, while the best performing model shows significant changes in only three, and some models show no significant changes at all. Regarding student performance, some models show feedback adaptivity between high and low performing students, but only in the feedback focus types they produce most frequently. To support future research, we release FeedType , a public corpus of annotated teacher and LLM feedback across three writing courses.

blocks.en: Appendix B Narciss’s Taxonomy and Our Adaptations
blocks.zh: 附录B 纳西斯的分类学和我们的适应

blocks.en: Narciss (2008a) proposes a content-based taxonomy of feedback components, distinguishing between simple and elaborated types. Simple feedback components include Knowledge of Performance (KP), Knowledge of Result (KR), and Knowledge of Correct Response (KCR). Elaborated feedback components include Knowledge about Task Constraints (KTC), Knowledge about Concepts (KC), Knowledge about Mistakes (KM), Knowledge about How to Proceed (KHP), and Knowledge about Metacognition (KMC). We adopt the elaborated feedback components as the basis for our feedback focus taxonomy, as they are more informative and better reflect the nature of writing feedback. Specifically, we retain Task Constraints, Concepts, and Mistakes, as these directly apply to writing tasks, mistakes in writing encompass a wide range of issues including grammar errors, organization, and coherence. We adapt KHP into Elaboration , as in writing feedback, procedural guidance typically takes the form of asking students to develop and expand their ideas. We adapt KCR into Clarification , as teachers often ask students to clarify their meaning rather than providing the correct response directly. We exclude the simple feedback components (KP, KR, KCR) as they are more suited to closed-ended tasks with clear correct answers, which does not apply to open-ended writing tasks. We also exclude KMC, as metacognitive feedback was rarely observed in our dataset. Finally, we add two categories not present in Narciss’s taxonomy: Praise , to capture positive reinforcement which is common in writing feedback, and Other , to account for feedback instances that address multiple focus types simultaneously or do not fit any type.
blocks.zh: Narciss(2008a)提出了基于内容的反馈元件分类法,区分简单和细化的类型. 简单的反馈组件包括性能知识(KP),结果知识(KR)和正确反应知识(KCR). 详细的反馈内容包括:关于任务限制的知识(KTC)、关于概念的知识(KC)、关于错误的知识(KM)、关于如何行事的知识(KHP)和关于元认知的知识(KMC)。 我们采用详尽的反馈部分作为我们反馈重点分类的基础,因为这些部分内容更加翔实,更好地反映了撰写反馈的性质。 具体地说,我们保留了任务限制、概念和错误,因为这些直接适用于写作任务,而书面错误包括一系列广泛的问题,包括语法错误、组织和一致性。 我们把KHP改编为Econdemination, 如书面反馈, 教师经常要求学生澄清其含义, 我们排除了简单的反馈组件(KP,KR,KCR),因为它们更适合有明确正确答案的封闭式任务,这不适用于开放式的写作任务. 我们还排除了知识管理中心,因为我们的数据集很少看到元认知反馈。 最后,我们增加Narciss分类学中没有的两个类别:赞美,以捕捉书面反馈中常见的正面强化,而其他,以考虑同时处理多个焦点类型或不适合任何类型的反馈。

blocks.en: Appendix D Evaluating LLMs as Annotators
blocks.zh: 附录D 将有限责任公司评为公证员

blocks.en: Our framework incorporates LLMs as part of the automatic evaluation procedure. To ensure the reliability of the LLM annotator, we verify three requirements in our evaluation procedure. First, we assess the reliability of the annotation task itself by collecting both human and model annotations on a subset of the data and computing inter-annotator agreement. This step confirms that the taxonomy is well-defined and that annotators can reach reasonable agreement on the evaluation outcomes. Second, following Calderon et al. (2025) , we evaluate whether the LLM can serve as a reliable substitute for human annotators. Third, we conduct a validity analysis to ensure that conclusions drawn from the full set of LLM-generated annotations are consistent with those derived from human annotations.
blocks.zh: 我们的框架将有限责任管理作为自动评价程序的一部分。 为确保LLM注释员的可靠性,我们核实我们评价程序中的三项要求。 首先,我们通过收集人文和模型说明数据子集以及计算注释人之间的协议来评估注释任务的可靠性。 这一步骤证实,分类学定义明确,注释员可以就评价结果达成合理的协议。 其次,继Calderon等人(2025年)之后,我们评价LLM是否能够作为人类注释者的可靠替代品。 第三,我们进行有效性分析,以确保从LLM产生的全套说明中得出的结论与从人类说明中得出的结论一致。

blocks.en: D.1 Traditional Metrics
blocks.zh: D.1 传统计量法

blocks.en: To compute inter-annotator agreement, we created a gold-standard reference dataset consisting of 100 feedback sampled from different essays. The sampled feedback covers multiple categories, with at least 10 examples per category, except for the Concepts category, which is less frequent in the dataset. The sample size was chosen to meet the evaluation of Alt-Test (see Subsection D.2 ), which requires at least 75 annotated instances to assess whether an alternative annotator can reliably replace human annotations. Three human annotators participated in labeling the reference dataset. Two annotators were involved in the initial development of the annotation guidelines, while a third annotator was added to satisfy the Alt-Test requirement of having at least three annotators. Before annotating the reference dataset, the third annotator was trained using the annotation guidelines, labeled 60 feedback from earlier pilot rounds, and resolved disagreements with one of the original annotators through discussion until consensus was reached. Agreement was evaluated on 40 new feedback selected from earlier pilot rounds, resulting in a Cohen’s Kappa of κ = 0.68 \kappa=0.68 . After this training, all three annotators annotated the full set of 100 feedback. After annotation, we used the human majority label for each feedback to calculate inter annotator agreement and accuracy. The majority label was defined as the label agreed upon by at least two annotators. If no agreement was reached, we followed the priority labeling rules described in Section C .

blocks.en: D.2 Alt-Test
blocks.zh: D.2 试验

blocks.en: The preceding group-level κ \kappa evaluation does not determine whether a specific LLM is comparable to a human annotator at the individual level, nor does it offer a principled threshold for trusting the model’s annotations. As a result, it cannot justify replacing human annotation with an LLM. To address this limitation, we employ the Alt-Test, which compares the LLM’s annotations to those of individual human annotators rather than to the group as a whole. We evaluate each candidate LLM against each of the three human annotators individually, using our gold-standard feedback subset described in D.1 . The test follows a leave-one-out approach, in which each human annotator is excluded in turn, and we evaluate whether the LLM’s annotations align more closely with the consensus of the remaining annotators than the excluded annotator does. For classification tasks, we use accuracy to measure alignment with the consensus. To account for the inherent variability and cost of human annotation, we introduce a tolerance margin ϵ \epsilon , allowing minor deviations, as implemented in the Alt-Test. Following prior work, ϵ \epsilon is selected based on annotator expertise: ϵ = 0.2 \epsilon=0.2 for experts, ϵ = 0.15 \epsilon=0.15 for skilled annotators, and ϵ = 0.1 \epsilon=0.1 for crowd workers. In our experiments, we observed that using larger ϵ \epsilon values (e.g., 0.15 and 0.2) led the models to pass the test across all settings in Table 10 . Therefore, to enforce a stricter evaluation criterion, we adopt ϵ = 0.1 \epsilon=0.1 , reflecting the relatively low-expertise nature of the task. If the LLM aligns better than the excluded annotator in more than half of the cases (winning rate > 0.5), it is considered a viable replacement for human annotation. As shown in Table 11 , the test yielded a winning rate of ω = 0.67 \omega=0.67 for Gemini Flash and GPT-4-Turbo with 10 few-shot examples, indicating that the LLM’s judgments can be reliably trusted. This result supports the use of the LLM as an annotator in our evaluation framework. So, we select Gemini 3 Flash as the annotator due to its lower cost compared to GPT-4-Turbo.
blocks.zh: 前面的团体级的“\kappa”评价并不能确定具体的LLM是否与个人级的人类注释员相比,也不能为信任模型的说明提供一个原则门槛。 因此,它不能作为用LLM代替人类注释的理由。 为了解决这一限制,我们采用了“阿尔特试验”,它将LLM的说明与个人注释员的说明比作整体说明。 我们利用D.1中描述的黄金标准反馈子集,逐个对照三个人的注释员对每个候选LLM进行评估。 测试采用的是“一放一放”的做法,即将每个人的注释排除在外,我们评价LLM的说明是否比被排除在外的注释者更接近其余注释者的共识。 对于分类任务,我们使用精确度来衡量与共识的一致性. 为了说明人类注解的内在变化和成本,我们引入了容忍比值 \\\epsilon,允许小偏差,在阿尔特测试中实施. 在之前的工作之后,QQ\\epsilon根据注释员的专业知识被选中:QQ=0.2\epsilon=0.2为专家,0.15\epsilon=0.15为熟练的注释员,QQ=0.1\epsilon=0.1为群众工人. 在我们的实验中,我们观察到,使用较大的\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\(如0.15和0.2)使模型在表10的所有设置中通过测试。 因此,为了执行更严格的评价标准,我们采用QQ=0.1\epsilon=0.1,反映了任务相对低专业知识的性质. 如果半数以上的案例(获奖率 > 0.5)的LLM比被排除在外的注释者配比更好,则这被认为是人类注释的一种可行的替代。 如表11所示,测试得出双子座闪电和GPT-4-Turbo的胜率为 QQ = 0.67\omega= 0.67,有10个几弹的例子,表明LLM的判断可以可靠地信赖. 这一结果支持在我们的评价框架中使用LLM作为注释员。 因此,我们选择双子座3 Flash作为注释员,因为它的成本比GPT-4-Turbo低.

blocks.en: D.3 LLM Annotation Validity
blocks.zh: D.3 LLM 注释有效性

blocks.en: The prior metrics used in subsections D.1 and D.2 do not guarantee that a model captures meaningful patterns in annotated data. As highlighted in prior work Thomas et al. (2025) , high agreement among annotators or strong performance on automated metrics does not necessarily reflect the validity of the annotations. In educational contexts, annotation quality should be evaluated based on whether it captures patterns that are meaningful, interpretable, and relevant to learning Thomas et al. (2025) . Motivated by this perspective, we move beyond agreement based evaluation and assess whether the model reflects educationally relevant patterns in feedback. We therefore evaluate the validity of the LLM as an annotator by examining whether its annotations capture meaningful and educationally relevant patterns, and whether they align with those observed in human annotated data. To do this, we select a subset of the dataset designed to capture variation in student performance across draft stages. For each assignment and draft stage (initial, revision, and final), we calculate the median score across all students and use it to distinguish higher and lower performing students. From each assignment at each draft stage, we select two essays with the highest scores and two with the lowest scores. With three assignments and three draft stages per assignment, this results in a total of 36 essays from Class 1. For each selected essay, we extract the corresponding teacher feedback and annotate it according to the categories defined in our taxonomy, resulting in a total of 441 feedback annotations. This sampling strategy aims to identify meaningful patterns to answer two research questions and support evaluation. First, what types of feedback change (increase or decrease) between drafts. Second, what types of feedback change for high versus low performing students?
blocks.zh: 第D.1和D.2小节中使用的以往的衡量标准并不能保证模型能够捕捉附加说明的数据中有意义的模式。 正如先前的工作托马斯等人(2025年)所强调的那样,注释者之间的高度一致或对自动化度量衡的强烈性能并不一定反映说明的有效性. 在教育方面,应当根据其是否掌握有意义、可解释和与学习托马斯等人有关的模式(2025年)来评价注释的质量。 从这一角度出发,我们超越了基于协议的评价,评估该模式在反馈中是否反映了与教育有关的模式。 因此,我们通过审查LLM的说明是否抓住了有意义的和教育相关的模式,以及它们是否与人类附加说明的数据中所观察到的模式相一致,来评价LLM作为注释者的有效性。 为此,我们选择了一个数据集的子集,该数据集旨在捕捉不同阶段学生表现的差异。 对于每个任务和起草阶段(初始、修订和最终阶段),我们计算所有学生的中位分,并用它来区分成绩优劣的学生。 从每个起草阶段的每个任务中,我们选择了两个成绩最高的散文和两个成绩最低的散文. 每期任务有三个任务和三个草稿阶段,这总共产生了36篇来自第1级的论文. 对于每篇选定的散文,我们提取相应的教师反馈,并按照分类学中定义的类别进行注释,结果总共产生了441份反馈说明. 这一抽样战略旨在确定有意义的模式,以回答两个研究问题并支持评价。 第一,草案之间有哪些类型的反馈变化(增加或减少)。 第二,高考生和低考生的反馈类型有什么变化?

blocks.en:
To address the first question, we examined the two most frequent feedback types, Praise and Task Constraints, that students received in the initial draft according to human annotations, tracked how their percentages changed across draft stages, and compared them with Gemini annotations for the same feedback types (see Table 12 ). Both human annotators and Gemini exhibited similar patterns: Praise feedback increased from the initial to final drafts, reflecting recognition of student improvements, while Task Constraint feedback decreased, indicating that students’ understanding of the assignment requirements improved across drafts. For student performance, addressing the second question, we followed a similar approach as in the first question. We focused on the two most frequent feedback types received by high performing students according to human annotations, Praise and Mistakes, and examined how their percentages changed between high and low performing students, as well as in Gemini annotations (see Table 13 ). Both human and Gemini annotations showed that Praise feedback decreased from high to low performing students, indicating that higher-performing students received more recognition. In contrast, Mistakes feedback increased, showing that lower performing students received more corrective feedback.
In both questions, Gemini was able to recognize the patterns identified by human annotations, as well as those reported in educational research on effective feedback practices as shown in Section 2 . In addition to capturing patterns observed in human annotations and the educational feedback literature, we compared the percentages of feedback categories between human annotations and Gemini. While the exact percentages were not always identical, Gemini generally reflected the trends seen in human annotations. Sometimes, however, Gemini was able to produce the same percentages. For example, the Praise category had very similar percentages in both the revision and final drafts, and categories such as Elaboration and Mistakes in the initial draft were also closely aligned.
blocks.zh:
为解决第一个问题,我们审查了学生在初步草案中根据人文说明收到的两种最经常的反馈类型,即 " 赞美 " 和 " 任务限制 " ,跟踪他们的百分比在草案阶段的变化情况,并就同样的反馈类型与双子座说明进行比较(见表12)。 人类注释员和双子座都表现出类似的模式: 赞美反馈从最初的草稿增加到最后的草稿,反映出对学生改进的认识,而Task Control反馈则减少,表明学生对分配要求的理解在草稿中都有改善。 关于学生的表现,处理第二个问题,我们采取了与第一个问题相似的做法。 我们侧重于高成绩学生根据人文说明收到的两种最经常的反馈类型,即赞美和错误,并审查了他们的百分比在高成绩和低成绩学生之间以及双子座说明中的变化(见表13)。 人文和双子座说明都表明,"颂"的反馈从高考生降至低考生,表明成绩较高的学生获得更多的认可. 相比之下,错误的反馈增加,表明表现较差的学生得到更多的纠正反馈.
在这两个问题中,双子座都能够认识到人类说明所查明的模式,以及在关于有效反馈做法的教育研究中所报告的模式,如第2节所示。 除了捕捉人类说明和教育反馈文献中观察到的规律外,我们还比较了人类说明和双子座之间反馈类别的百分比. 虽然确切的百分比并不总是相同的,但双子座一般反映了人类说明中的趋势。 然而,有时双子座可以得出同样的百分比。 例如, " 颂 " 类在修订稿和最后草案中的百分比非常相似,初步草案中的阐述和错误等类别也非常一致。

blocks.en: We prompt the models under three conditions to generate feedback on student essay paragraphs. In all conditions, the model is provided with the entire essay, the target paragraph, the assignment rubric, and the draft stage. For revision and final drafts, previously received feedback is also included so the model can consider prior comments when generating updated feedback. Prompt 1 (Zero-shot): The model receives no information about feedback focus types and is prompted to generate feedback directly. Prompt 2 (Zero-shot + Categories): The model additionally receives the names and definitions of the seven feedback focus types to guide its output. Prompt 3 (Few-shot + Categories): The model receives the names, definitions, and examples of each feedback focus type to further guide its output. blocks.en: We prompt the models in both zero shot and few shot settings to evaluate feedback on student essay paragraphs by classifying it into one of seven predefined categories. The prompt includes the list of these seven categories along with their definitions and rubric, as well as the target paragraph and the corresponding feedback to be annotated. For the few shot setting, we construct examples using newly selected data from Class 1, annotated by the first author. Specifically, we include at least 10 examples for each feedback category, except for the Concept category, which is relatively rare in our dataset. In total, 85 annotated feedback instances are used as examples to guide the annotation task. Table 14 shows the prompt conditions used for feedback classification.
